To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GABAA receptor activation evoked whole-cell currents in neurons from the nucleus of the tractus solitarius (NTS) of hypertensive (HT) rats, but not normotensive (N) rats.
responses to GABAA-receptors activation are altered in neurons isolated from the nucleus of the tractus solitarius of renal-wrap hypertensive rats.
the EC50 of GABAA evoked currents in NTS neurons was significantly increased in neurons from renal-wrapped hypertensive rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that afferent inputs to NTS neurons play in the development of hypertension.
the role of GABA in the nucleus of solitary tract (NT) in renal-wrapped hypertension.
the mechanisms of hypertension and the role of the nucleus of the tractus solitarius (NTS) in mediating this disease process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GABAA receptor is not altered in HT.
GABAA receptor responses are altered in NTS neurons isolated from renal-wrapping hypertension, but the functional significance is unknown.
the responses of NTS neurons to activation of GABA receptors are altered in the hypertensive state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GABAergic inhibitory neurotransmission is reduced in the NTS of renal-wrap hypertensive rats, and the GABA receptor-mediated inhibitory currents are reduced in magnitude and duration.
GABAA receptor responses in the NTS are altered in HT and that these alterations may influence afferent processing in this brainstem nucleus.
the GABAA receptor function is altered in the NTS of hypertensive animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are changes in the function of the GABA receptor in the NTS of renal wrap hypertensive rats.
GABAA receptors in NTS are altered in HT, and this could contribute to the altered afferent processing that occurs in HT.
the GABAA receptor function is altered in hypertension.
